In a dark theme `$secondary` is the dark background color, so both the text and the badge background are dark, making the badge count unreadable. This changes the light-theme color from a relatively dark gray to a very light gray, making embedded-post author links much fainter than before and inconsistent with similar username links that preserve 30% for light themes. The likely intended value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`."

This mobile change uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which changes the light-theme appearance and makes mobile inconsistent with desktop. The values appear to have been inverted accidentally."

The desktop version preserves 20% for light themes and uses 80% secondary for dark themes, but this mobile change uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. That changes the light-theme heading color and reduces contrast relative to the intended styling."

findings.title: Dark notification badge background is paired with dark `$secondary` text
findings.body: `.badge-notification` keeps `color: $secondary` (and `&[href] { color: $secondary; }`) while the new dark-theme background becomes `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. In a dark theme `$secondary` is the dark background color, so both the text and the badge background are dark, making the badge count unreadable. Before this change the dark-theme background was derived from `$primary`, which would be light. The text color or background needs to be adapted for dark themes.

findings.title: Embedded-post author link light-theme color changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: The diff replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This changes the light-theme color from a relatively dark gray to a very light gray, making embedded-post author links much fainter than before and inconsistent with similar username links that preserve 30% for light themes. The likely intended value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length uses inverted light/dark lightness values
findings.body: The original rule used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the desktop modal counterpart preserves that light value with a dark value of 30%. This mobile change uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which changes the light-theme appearance and makes mobile inconsistent with desktop. The values appear to have been inverted accidentally.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original mobile style for `.topic-map h3` used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The desktop version preserves 20% for light themes and uses 80% secondary for dark themes, but this mobile change uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. That changes the light-theme heading color and reduces contrast relative to the intended styling.

findings.title: Category badge notification color still uses unconverted `scale-color($primary)`
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, while the rest of the PR converts comparable `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` colors to `dark-light-choose(... scale-color($secondary ...))`. This missed occurrence means dark themes will not use the secondary-derived color, leaving this badge text inconsistent with the rest of the updated styles.
